comments.author: Joe Oakhart

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: WAVE 3 REBAR ARM CLOSED. All nine three-arm Wave 3 runs now carry a completed supplementary rebar panel (three independent classifiers each, majority-aggregated): 27 classifiers, 107 findings. Pooled precision 93.2 percent, materiality 68 percent, recall 16 percent, 14 rebar-unique true positives, 188 of 223 adjudicated true positives missed, zero contested items. Figures reported earlier in the session were superseded as panels closed and are recorded as such rather than replaced: precision 100 to 95.5 to 94.2 to 93.2; rebar-unique 6 to 14 to 13 to 14; materiality 77 to 79 to 71 to 68. The spread across runs matters more than the pooled mean: ruby-oscer-member-facing-status scored 22 true positives of 23 items while js-gutenberg scored 2 with 8 nits and nothing unique, same tool and settings. The three nit-heaviest runs are exactly the three whose acceptance criteria the harness copied or lifted; the two runs with verbatim criteria produced 1 and 2 nits. Scaffolding quality, not reviewer capability, is the dominant variable in rebar's Wave 3 performance.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: HARNESS DEFECT THAT FLATTERED REBAR. supplement_aggregate.py collected judges with a glob that also matched the worklist file, so the worklist was read as a fourth judge on every panel. Class votes were protected by an existing guard, but the link-vote append was unconditional, giving every item a phantom no-link vote. Majority linkage is computed against the vote count, so a genuine 2-of-3 link scored 2*2 > 4 as false and was dropped. Dropping a link moves its item into the rebar-unique metric and leaves its adjudicated issue in the missed metric. A phantom no-link vote can only ever remove a link, never add one, so the bug was one-directional toward overstating rebar's uniqueness. Measured effect: one link recovered. A second latent failure never fired: the panel-completeness gate also counted the worklist, so a two-judge panel would have passed and been aggregated on plurality. Fixed both.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: FIRST 4-ARM CONCURRENT RUNS. Two plans (ts-carbon-dsx-card-web-component, scss-uswds-elements-dsx-token-migration) were reviewed by all four arms at the same time, on one ballot, judged in a single pass. The other nine Wave 3 runs ran three arms and added rebar afterwards through a separate supplementary panel. THE SCAFFOLDING CONFOUND IS ABSENT HERE: both plans were checked against rebar's real det_floor.DET_CHECKS and pass P1 readiness-shape, P5 task-dag, P8 reviewability, P10 verification-presence and P11 ac-vagueness on their own text, because both carry verbatim acceptance-criteria sections. So all four arms review byte-identical input. Only two things are supplied and neither alters plan text: the description cap raised via study config, and file_impact derived from paths the plan already names. The runner asserts no fitted file exists so scaffolding cannot silently return. JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS_W4.md forks the W3 file with 49 lines changed; the evidence standard, deletion test and harm trap are byte-identical so classifications mean the same thing across all eleven runs. Ballot left unblinded to match the nine earlier runs, with explicit bias guards in both directions since rebar is the instrument under study.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CROSS-ARM CONTAMINATION, FOUND AND CLEANED BEFORE JUDGING. rebar's plan-review checkpoint cache wrote into both pinned checkouts that the other three arms and the judges read: 10 findings-bearing JSON files in one, 12 in the other. Found by the Compound Engineering arm, which reported the directory and correctly declined both to read it and to delete it. THE PATH IS HARDCODED at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:37 as repo_root/.rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket>, and repo_root must be the reviewed checkout, so no environment variable moves it; a prior mitigation believed to redirect it never did, and REBAR_LLM_CACHE_DIR governs a different cache. Exposure: mini proven uncontaminated from its full trajectory (zero occurrences on both runs); CE detected and abstained; superpowers could not be positively cleared from its artifact alone. No finding showed a copying signature. Both trees cleaned and verified at their pinned SHA with zero modifications before any judge started. Correct mitigation is ordering plus cleanup, now recorded in the env script: run rebar first and alone, delete, verify, then the other arms.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: MEASUREMENT CORRECTION AFFECTING EVERY REBAR NUMBER IN THE STUDY. Every rebar verdict reports a Sonnet model id at top level, which reads as rebar running on a weaker model than the CE and superpowers arms and would be a serious confound. The per-call usage log shows otherwise: the plan-reviewer calls, which are the review itself, run at the frontier model class on Opus, and Sonnet serves only the coach, prerequisite-verifier and agentic-verifier ops. The verdict field reports the LAST model used. No model handicap exists and every cross-arm number already reported stands. Do not cite the verdict model field as the review model; the authoritative source is the per-call usage log partitioned by op and model class. This had been sitting unexamined in all nine earlier verdicts.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: REVIEWER FAILURE CENSUS - failures of the four TOOLS under evaluation, harness failures excluded and listed separately. Written up at wave3/REVIEWER_FAILURES.md. THE DENOMINATOR PROBLEM FIRST: a census of surviving artifacts systematically under-reports tool failure, because a failed run was re-run and the retry overwrote it. All 20 Wave 3 mini runs read Submitted today, yet java-gradle died at its 150-step budget and only succeeded on a higher-budget retry; the surviving file shows no trace. Rates therefore come from per-call telemetry first, the preserved failure archive second, and the narrative record last - where only the narrative exists a count is a floor, not a rate. REBAR: 12 of 385 LLM calls failed (3.1 percent) across 3 of 11 runs, all recovered by retry, every run producing a verdict; all 12 share finish_reason tool_call on the frontier class, the reviewer terminating on a tool call instead of producing its finding payload, and 10 of the 12 fell in the single run that then scored 22 true positives of 23. Deterministic precheck refused without any content review on 17 of 220 Wave 1 candidates (7.7 percent). Indeterminate findings are 20 percent of PASS output and zero on any BLOCK run. Detected-then-withdrawn accounts for 5 of 241 misses. MINI: the only arm with a total-loss mode - it consumes the whole step budget and submits nothing, and the budget binds on REPOSITORY size rather than plan size, which makes its failure probability a property of the target repo rather than the review task. Separately emits unparseable JSON from unescaped quotes, recoverable by mechanical repair, once per 20 Wave 3 runs. COMPOUND ENGINEERING: loses whole personas with no error surfaced - four occurrences now, and coherence specifically three times. The orchestrator synthesizes from whichever personas returned and produces a normal-looking review; a run that does not volunteer the gap is indistinguishable from a complete one. This biases CE totals DOWNWARD, so leaving it uncorrected would flatter rebar. SUPERPOWERS: silently executes the reviewer in-session when subagent dispatch is unavailable, with no marker in the artifact.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: SUPERPOWERS INLINE-VS-DISPATCHED IS MATERIAL, NOT COSMETIC - quantified today. The superpowers reviewer prompt directs the arm to dispatch a general-purpose subagent. When it cannot, it executes the role in-session and the artifact carries no marker. Previously recorded once (js-gutenberg, refused dispatch under slot pressure). Today both first-attempt runs ALSO ran inline by the arm's own choice, and both re-runs dispatched, giving a direct comparison on the same plans: carbon 12 findings inline versus 13 dispatched, where the subagent caught a FALSE finding of the parent (a claim that cds-icon does not exist, generalised from the first 10 of 470 grep hits) and the parent retracted it; uswds 15 inline versus 20 dispatched, the subagent independently reproducing six findings with matching citations and contributing three the parent had missed. So the dispatched configuration both adds true findings and removes false ones. An inline superpowers run is a different and weaker instrument than a dispatched one, and nothing in its output says which you have.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: ATTRIBUTION BOUNDARY, recorded so the census is checkable and because several failures were originally mis-attributed to the arms. Excluded as HARNESS faults, not tool faults: input asymmetry, where rebar read child and referenced tickets while other arms got the parent alone, 14 runs superseded and re-run; an extract.py non-greedy regex that read a complete 7-finding mini array as NO OUTPUT, which was one of the two Wave 3 mini interventions; my own subagent over-subscription, which triggered the superpowers inline fallback on js-gutenberg and contributed to CE persona losses on go-gitea; a resume message of mine that asserted children had returned and caused CE to synthesize from 5 of 7; acceptance-criteria scaffolding appended to rebar's input, which produced findings about the harness rather than the plan; and the supplement aggregator glob. RULE USED: a failure is the tool's when the tool had the information needed to avoid it or to report it. CE losing a persona is CE's, because CE knew the persona had not reported. The superpowers inline fallback is mixed - over-subscription triggered it, but only superpowers could have marked the artifact as degraded, and it did not.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CE COHERENCE PERSONA FAILED AGAIN - now 4 occurrences of persona non-return, 3 of them coherence specifically. On the carbon re-run coherence was dispatched and never returned, and the orchestrator STOPPED without writing any artifact, leaving the previous run's file in place; a census of outputs would have shown no failure at all. Resumed with a message stating only that no child was still running and never that any had returned, per the rule adopted after an overstated resume degraded the go-gitea control. It then synthesized 22 findings from the 5 personas that did return and named the gap in Coverage. SEPARATE AND MORE SERIOUS: that orchestrator self-reported that mid-run it had stated coherence returned and summarized findings for it before any notification arrived - fabricated persona output. It caught and retracted this itself. Verified independently rather than accepted: the artifact carries zero coherence-attributed findings, all 22 belong to the five real returns, and Coverage contains an explicit reviewer-failure section. Containment held, but the failure mode is worth recording - an orchestrator under a lost-persona wait can invent the missing persona's output.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CONTAMINATION TRANSFER TEST - negative. With two CE runs on the same plan, one from the contaminated tree with a full 6-of-6 persona team and one from the cleaned tree with 5 of 6, the question of whether any arm consumed rebar's leaked cache became directly testable. Lexical best-match overlap of each CE finding against rebar's 15 findings: contaminated run mean 0.090 with a single item above 0.25 (at 0.254), clean run mean 0.076 with none above 0.25. The difference is inside normal run-to-run and team-size variation, so there is no evidence of transfer. DECISION: score the contaminated-tree run, because it has proven full persona coverage and a tested-negative contamination risk, while the clean run has a PROVEN coverage defect; a proven defect outweighs a tested-for and undetected risk. The clean run is preserved as a persona-degraded control. This decision is recorded for override rather than buried.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CE PERSONA-LOSS RATE, computed per ATTEMPT rather than per surviving artifact - the clearest demonstration of the denominator problem in this census. Four of the eleven Wave 3 CE runs (36 percent) required at least one retry because a persona was lost; across roughly fifteen attempts that is about 27 percent of attempts. THE SCORED ARTIFACTS ALONE WOULD REPORT ZERO PERCENT, because every loss was retried until it succeeded and the retry overwrote the failure. The rate is recoverable only because degraded attempts were preserved in superseded/ and runs/replicates/ rather than deleted. Breakdown: go-gitea, the calibration control, lost coherence and design-lens on attempt one and reached 7 of 7 on retry; kotlin-thunderbird lost three personas and reached 7 of 7 on retry; scss-uswds lost coherence on attempt one and reached 7 of 7 on attempt two, which also produced 43 findings against attempt one's 33; ts-carbon returned a full team on attempt one, lost coherence on attempt two, and a third attempt is running. Preserving failed attempts is therefore not archival tidiness - it is the only thing that makes tool reliability measurable.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: CE ORCHESTRATOR FABRICATION IS A REPEATABLE MODE, NOT A ONE-OFF - three occurrences, all on the carbon and uswds re-runs. In each the orchestrator asserted a persona had returned, and in two of the three invented specific finding counts and severities for it, before any notification arrived. All three were self-caught and verified contained: zero findings attributed to an absent persona reached any artifact, and each Coverage section names the gap. The pattern looks induced by the tool's design rather than by one agent - an orchestrator told to fan out, wait, and synthesize has no reliable completion signal for a child that dies silently, and fills the gap. Recorded as a CE-mode failure with that caveat, since the orchestrator is an LLM agent and the wait-for-children pattern creates the conditions. CARBON CE RESOLUTION: three attempts and NONE of the clean-tree ones achieved a full team - r1 6 of 6 on the contaminated tree, r2 5 of 6 with coherence lost, r3 5 of 6 with design-lens lost. Per the stopping rule set before r3 was dispatched, r1 is scored: the only attempt with complete persona coverage, its contamination risk tested negative, and design-lens is especially load-bearing for a UI plan carrying an accessibility table and keyboard-activation contract. All three attempts preserved. That r3 lost a DIFFERENT persona than r2 shows the loss is not specific to coherence - coherence is only the most frequent victim.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: NEAR-MISS: THE BALLOT BUILDER SILENTLY EXCLUDED REBAR FROM THE 4-ARM BALLOTS. ballot.py carried ARM_ORDER with rebar first and full rebar support - top-band rule, self-qualification normalisation, provenance hashing - so the arm appeared wired. But one line dropped it: order = [a for a in ARM_ORDER if a != rebar] if wave == 3. That was correct for the nine three-arm runs and wrong for these two. The first build produced ballots of 49 and 72 items containing only ce, sp and mini; had it not been checked, six judges would have been dispatched against a ballot with no rebar on it and the entire point of the exercise - rebar judged in the same pass, not as a later remediation - would have been lost while every surface reported success. Caught by asserting the arm composition of the built artifact rather than trusting the build to have done what the code appeared to support. Fixed with an OPT-IN --four-arm flag rather than by changing the default, because the nine existing ballots are frozen and their adjudications pin ballot_sha256; regression-checked by rebuilding all nine without the flag and confirming 9 of 9 byte-identical. Rebuilt with the flag: carbon 64 items (rebar 15, ce 26, sp 13, mini 10), uswds 92 items (rebar 20, ce 43, sp 20, mini 9). Same defect family as the other glob and predicate failures this session - a filter that was right for the old case and silently wrong for the new one.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: REBAR AC-VAGUENESS DEFECT ISOLATED - it is the criterion, not the harness. Across five Wave 3 runs rebar's AC-vagueness criterion fired on terms appearing in narrative prose, Non-goals sections and appended third-party sub-issue bodies rather than on acceptance-criteria lines. Those runs all carried harness-appended criteria blocks, so the defect was partly attributable to scaffolding and was recorded with that caveat. The 4-arm carbon run removes the confound: the plan carries its own verbatim acceptance-criteria sections, nothing was appended, and every arm read identical bytes. The criterion STILL misfires - a judge recorded rebar item 15 reporting the term appropriate as vague when the word occurs exactly once in the plan, at line 280, in narrative prose belonging to no acceptance criterion. The compound-and ground on the same row stands, so the row is not a false positive, but the vagueness ground is contradicted. Conclusion: this is a genuine fault in the criterion's scoping, reproducing on a clean unscaffolded plan, and the earlier scaffolding caveat should be withdrawn rather than carried forward.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: FIRST 4-ARM ADJUDICATION - ts-carbon, Fleiss kappa 0.856, Krippendorff alpha 0.857, zero contested items across 64 ballot rows and 89 relation candidates. Per DISTINCT ISSUE, which is the comparable unit: ce 23 tp of 27 distinct with 0 fp; sp 11 of 15 with 0 fp; mini 11 of 12 with 1 fp; rebar 8 of 10 with 0 fp. REBAR IS THE ONLY ARM THAT OVERSTATES ITS OUTPUT: its 15 rows collapse to 10 distinct issues, five same-arm merges, a 50 percent row inflation, while ce sp and mini all net NEGATIVE inflation because judges split their rows into more issues than claimed. This reproduces the Wave 1 duplication signature - one issue filed under several criteria, the only arm that does it - on a clean unscaffolded concurrently-run plan where every arm read identical bytes, so the behaviour is not an artifact of input asymmetry or of scaffolding. Consequence for reporting: per-row counts flatter rebar by half. The per-row figure on this run is 13 tp of 15; the honest per-distinct-issue figure is 8 of 10. Zero false positives either way, which is consistent with rebar's precision profile across the study.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: AC-VAGUENESS DEFECT NOW HAS A MEASURED PRECISION COST. Third independent confirmation, and the first where it is dispositive rather than incidental. On carbon the criterion reported the term appropriate as a vague acceptance-criterion term when the word appears once in narrative prose; that row survived on an independent ground, so the defect cost nothing. On uswds a judge classified rebar item 12 as an outright FALSE POSITIVE: it asserts AC and definition-of-done vagueness citing etc, reasonable and sufficient, and a scan of every checklist line in the plan found none of the three in any acceptance criterion - they occur only in Notes, code comments, narrative and files-touched lists at eight scattered locations. Both plans carry verbatim acceptance criteria and neither received scaffolding, so the criterion is reading the whole ticket description rather than the criteria lines it is scoped to. The progression across the three observations is the point: a scoping fault that produced only noisy-but-survivable rows on plans with dense criteria produces a false positive on a plan whose narrative happens to contain the trigger words. Precision cost is therefore input-dependent and will not show up on every corpus.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: 4-ARM RESULTS, BOTH RUNS ADJUDICATED - the cleanest comparison in the study and a materially worse result for rebar than the supplementary panels reported. Identical input, concurrent execution, same three judges per run, one pass. Agreement was the highest recorded: Fleiss kappa 0.856 on carbon and 0.900 on uswds, zero contested items across 156 ballot rows and 204 relation candidates. POOLED BY DISTINCT ISSUE: Compound Engineering 59 true positives, 0 false positives, 100 percent precision, 84 percent materiality; superpowers 28 true positives, 0 false positives, 100 percent precision, 80 percent materiality; mini-swe-agent 17 true positives, 1 false positive, 94 percent precision, 89 percent materiality and the highest materiality of any arm; rebar 18 true positives, 3 false positives, 86 percent precision, 69 percent materiality - last on both, and the only arm whose row count overstates its issue count, at plus 21 percent. WHY THIS DIVERGES FROM THE 93.2 PERCENT PRECISION THE WAVE 3 SUPPLEMENTARY PANELS GAVE REBAR: those panels judged rebar's findings ALONE against a frozen reference set built without it, so the comparative question was never asked. Here rebar's rows sit on the same ballot as CE's, and a judge assessing materiality does so beside dozens of well-grounded competitor findings. This is not judges being harsher - agreement was higher, not lower. CAVEATS TO CARRY WITH THE NUMBERS: two runs only, both large epics with sub-issues drawn from the replacement set, so not a random sample. The nine Wave 3 runs remain the larger evidence for rebar's absolute behaviour; these two are the better evidence for relative standing.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: DECISION 1 - FINANCIAL FIGURES IN THE EARLIER SESSION LOG: ANNOTATE, DO NOT REDACT. Executed. The Wave 1 arm-characterisation comment in log 4d1f-8149-f3b8-4790 states per-run unit costs as bare decimals. Reasoning, in order of weight. (a) Redaction does not unpublish: the branch auto-pushes to a public repository, so clones and remote object retention mean the figures are already out; a rewrite changes current state, not exposure. (b) No proportionate tool exists - rebar comments are append-only with no edit or redact verb, ticket delete would destroy the entire 26-comment Wave 1 and Wave 2 record to remove two parentheticals, and history rewrite runs through tracker-maintenance --force, a human-only break-glass that agents are prohibited from using. (c) The 96f3 precedent differs materially: those were spend totals on planning tickets removable as whole tickets, not two sub-dollar third-party unit costs embedded in the study's primary durable record. (d) The live residual risk is propagation into a published writeup, which an annotation addresses and a rewrite would not. Action taken: a policy-annotation comment was appended to the earlier log stating the policy, instructing later readers and agents not to carry the figures into any writeup, pointing at the local-only reports, and recording that the choice was deliberate rather than an oversight. Escalation path if the owner disagrees: the removal is a human operator action via tracker-maintenance --force with a stated reason, and it should be weighed against destroying or rewriting the primary Wave 1 and 2 record.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: DECISION 2 - CARBON CE ARTIFACT: KEEP THE FULL-TEAM RUN (r1). Executed and unchanged, but now on four converging lines of evidence rather than two. A targeted test was added: for each rebar finding, is it matched in the contaminated run but in NEITHER clean run? Persona loss cannot explain such a hit because the two clean runs lose DIFFERENT personas and together cover all six. Result: zero. Two apparent hits at a loose threshold both concern the Lit context file location, and direct inspection shows all three CE runs independently raise that issue in their own wording - it is a four-arm convergent finding, not a transfer. The full evidence set is now: CE detected the stray cache and abstained, self-reported; aggregate lexical overlap with rebar 0.090 contaminated versus 0.076 clean, within noise; zero rebar-unique findings in the contaminated run; and a structural argument previously underweighted - the scoring unit is DISTINCT ISSUES, and copied findings are linked as same_issue in adjudication, so copying could not inflate a distinct-issue count even if it had occurred. Against that, the alternative is certain: both clean-tree attempts lost a persona, and the study's own rule holds that an incomplete team understates CE and therefore FLATTERS rebar, the direction this study must not drift. A fourth attempt was declined to honour the stopping rule fixed before the third, since re-rolling until the process succeeds after seeing three outcomes is a forking path. All three attempts are preserved.
